name: sugi
why: The Sugi Pharmacy receipt as printed: two item discounts, an 8% discount on the four items without one (base 2,909) and points on the whole receipt. The finals reproduce the printed tax bases (5,573 and 236).

adjustments.label: スギポイント値引金額

name: sugi_subset_discount_read_as_the_line_above
why: The dominant misread today: the 8% line is attached to the snack printed above it. The printed base recovers the four items.

adjustments.label: スギポイント値引金額

name: sugi_subset_discount_without_its_base
why: The base line is missing: the 8% still fits only the items without an item discount (8% of 2,909 is 232.72).

adjustments.label: スギポイント値引金額

name: sugi_item_discount_read_under_the_wrong_item
why: Seen live: the second 15% line attached to the mask. 15% of 767 is 115, so the one item it fits (1,958) is used instead.

adjustments.label: スギポイント値引金額

name: sugi_both_item_discounts_read_under_one_item
why: Both 15% lines on item 3: the second fits item 3 only after its first discount (15% of 1,963 is 294.45) while it fits item 4 as printed, so the receipt is ambiguous and nothing is allocated.

adjustments.label: スギポイント値引金額

name: sugi_points_line_dropped_shopping_total_read
why: Points dropped and the shopping total 6,303 read as the amount due. Items and total agree, but the printed taxable bases add up to 5,809, 494 less.

name: sugi_points_line_dropped
why: Points dropped, amount due read correctly: the items come to 6,303 against 5,809.

name: sugi_total_before_points_read
why: The shopping total 6,303 read as the amount due while the points line is present: the total paid is 6,303 less the points.

adjustments.label: スギポイント値引金額

name: sugi_points_transcribed_before_the_subset_discount
why: Order swap: with points first, no set of items costs 2,909 when the 8% line is reached, so the receipt is flagged instead of reconciling up to 6 yen off per item.

adjustments.label: スギポイント値引金額

name: sugi_item_numbers_repeated
why: The model numbered every item 1, so its hints mean nothing. Items are numbered by position and the printed percentages find the items.

adjustments.label: スギポイント値引金額

name: item_and_subset_discounts_with_points
why: Archetype A: the Sugi shape on other numbers. お買物合計 3,356; bases 2,851 and 255.

name: bundle_discount_on_named_items
why: Archetype C: a 50 yen multi-buy on the two cans, taken from the items the model names.

name: amount_only_discount_with_no_items_named
why: Archetype C without a hint: nothing printed says which items, so it is spread over the whole receipt and marked assumed for review.

name: percent_discount_printed_after_its_item
why: Archetype D1: 30% off the sashimi printed directly under it.

name: percent_discount_printed_before_its_item
why: Archetype D2: the line sits under the bread but 30% of 158 is 47, so it belongs to the sashimi.

name: points_printed_as_a_payment_with_the_total_before_points
why: Archetype F (NTA example): points paid after 合計 1,090. Points still reduce what the group splits, so the total is 1,069.

name: points_printed_as_a_payment_with_the_amount_paid
why: Archetype F with the electronic-money payment 1,069 read as the amount due.

name: service_charge_with_tax_added_on_top
why: Archetype G: a 10% service charge, then 10% tax on 19,085 added on top. Costs stay before tax and the app adds the rate, as for such receipts today.

name: discount_larger_than_its_item
why: Archetype H: a 150 yen coupon under a 108 yen tea. It cannot be the tea's alone, so a person decides.

name: coupon_on_a_single_item_receipt
why: Archetype I: with one item there is only one possible scope.

name: free_item_then_member_discount
why: Archetype J: a free-coffee coupon, then 5% member discount on what is left (380). The free item stays listed at 0.

name: coupon_before_tax_in_cents
why: A cents currency: a 2.50 coupon over the receipt, then 8.25% tax added on 22.98.

name: whole_dollar_amounts_keep_cents
why: Every printed amount is whole but the currency has cents, so the coupon is split to the cent.

name: cents_printed_while_decimal_places_read_as_zero
why: The model said 0 decimal places but printed cents, so the cents win.

name: no_adjustments_tax_included
why: A plain receipt that works today keeps working unchanged.

name: no_adjustments_tax_added_on_top
why: A plain tax-exclusive receipt keeps today's shape: prices before tax plus the rate.

name: no_adjustments_mixed_rates_tax_included
why: Mixed 8% and 10% with tax inside the prices: the rate shown is the one with the larger base.

name: no_adjustments_with_a_misread_total
why: Nothing to allocate, but the items do not add up to the amount due.

name: coupon_with_mixed_rates_and_tax_added_on_top
why: Archetype B: tax added on top at 8% and 10%. The printed bases single out each rate's items (1,279 is the beef and milk, 512 the detergent), so each rate's tax goes into its own items: 1,096 + 87, 183 + 15, 512 + 51.

name: discount_larger_than_the_receipt
why: A coupon worth more than everything bought: whatever items it covers, the receipt cannot add up (100 - 150 is not 1), so it is read again rather than sent to a review that cannot succeed.

name: base_matched_by_two_sets_of_items
why: 300 is both the third item and the first two: the printed base cannot say which.

name: base_and_percentage_disagree
why: The base matches two items, but 10% of 300 is 30, not 50: one of the printed numbers was misread.

name: percentage_that_fits_two_identical_items
why: Two 980 yen items and 30% off one of them, with no item named.

name: percentage_that_fits_two_identical_items_one_named
why: The same receipt with the item named: the printed placement decides.

name: percentage_that_fits_nothing
why: 15% fits no item and no set of items.

name: receipt_wide_percent_discount
why: 10% off everything, with no base printed.

name: percent_discount_on_named_items
why: A set discount whose percent fits the two items named together.

name: second_discount_on_the_same_item
why: Two discounts on one item: the second is 10% of what the item costs after the first (900), and no other item fits.

name: base_recovered_by_subset_search
why: The base 1,250 is none of the simple candidates; exactly one set of items (500 + 750) costs that much.

name: base_matched_by_no_items
why: A misread base (2,900 for 2,909) that no set of items costs.

name: surcharge_on_named_items
why: A container fee printed under two items, with nothing else to check it against.

name: hints_to_items_that_do_not_exist_are_ignored
why: The model names item 9 on a two-item receipt; the discount falls back to the whole receipt.

name: zero_amount_lines_and_meaningless_numbers_are_dropped
why: A zero discount line is skipped, a percent above 100 and a zero base are ignored, and a negative tax rate is not a rate.

name: several_rates_without_bases_show_no_rate
why: Two rates printed with no taxable bases: no single rate to show.

name: tax_bases_with_their_tax_add_up_to_the_total
why: Tax-exclusive bases printed with their tax: the bases plus tax are the total, which agrees.

name: tax_bases_that_disagree_without_tax_amounts
why: The bases are printed but not the tax amounts, and the bases match nothing.

name: tax_amount_printed_without_a_rate
why: The T-shirt receipt: Tax 10.00 with no rate on a 69.40 subtotal. There is no rate for the app to add, so the tax is spread over the items in proportion (2.87, 1.43, 5.70).

name: printed_tax_rate_that_does_not_fit_the_items
why: Archetype E: 8.25% of 20.35 is 1.68, but 1.52 is printed because the bananas are tax-exempt. Spreading the tax over every item would misprice them, so it goes to review.

name: coupon_with_the_subtotal_before_it_read_as_amount_due
why: The model lists a 100 coupon but copies the subtotal before it (1,050) as the amount due. The printed prices add up to that total, so they must not be returned as costs: the app would file the full price.

name: both_item_discounts_read_under_one_item_with_two_rivals
why: The second 15% line fits item 1 only after its first discount, while two 1,958 items fit it as printed. Ambiguous, so a person decides.

name: two_equal_items_both_discounts_read_under_the_first
why: Two 1,958 items, each with a 15% line, both read under the first. The second fits item 1 as printed, but item 1 already has its own discount and item 2, which has none, fits too.

name: two_equal_items_second_discount_without_a_hint
why: The same receipt with no item named for the second line: both 1,958 items fit as printed, but only the undiscounted one fits what it costs now.

name: sugi_points_dropped_with_a_base_printed_without_a_rate
why: Points dropped and 6,303 read as the total, with the one tax line read as a base without a rate. That base (5,809) still shows 494 is missing.

name: tax_inside_the_prices_is_not_added_again
why: The printed tax (90 on a base of 1,000) is 10/110 of the base, so it is inside the prices; a misread amount due of 1,100 must not be explained by adding 10% on top.

name: points_after_tax_on_a_tax_exclusive_receipt
why: Tax added on top (100 on 1,000), then 100 of points paid after tax. Points equal to the tax make the items less points look like the amount paid, but the base says the prices exclude tax: a deduction after tax, which goes to review.

name: prices_before_tax_with_the_subtotal_read_as_amount_due
why: Tax added on top (100 on 1,000) but the subtotal before tax read as the amount due: items and total agree, yet the printed tax line says 100 is missing.

name: fully_paid_with_points
why: Points cover the whole receipt and the model copied the total before them: a total of 0 is not something to split.

name: display_rate_follows_the_largest_base_per_rate
why: The 10% items print on two lines (300 + 300), more than the single 8% line (500).

name: bundle_then_percent_off_everything_else
why: A multi-buy on the two cans, then 8% off the rest (72 is 8% of 900): the bundle's items count as already discounted.

name: percent_rounded_line_by_line
why: 5% of the printed base 1,050 is 52.5, but 48 is printed (each line rounded down). A percent is taken on its printed base, so the line goes to a person rather than trusting whichever items fit.

name: tax_amount_that_fits_neither_form_says_nothing
why: A tax amount (50 on 1,000) that is neither 10% of the base nor 10/110 of it, likely misread: it decides nothing about whether prices include tax.

name: tax_base_covering_only_part_of_the_items
why: Tax added on top to a base of 1,000 while the items come to 1,200: the printed tax line does not account for the receipt, so it goes to review.

name: per_rate_bases_that_do_not_single_out_items
why: Tax on top at 8% and 10% on bases of 300 each: 300 is both the third item and the first two, so neither rate's items are known.

name: sugi_with_one_tax_base_unread
why: The 10% base was not transcribed, so the bases cannot be checked; the receipt still reconciles on its total.

adjustments.label: スギポイント値引金額

name: tax_without_base_and_the_subtotal_read_as_amount_due
why: US layout: TAX 8.25% 2.48 with no base, and the subtotal 30.00 read as the amount due. 2.48 is 8.25% of 30.00 added on top, not tax inside it, so the reading is refused.

name: tax_without_base_read_correctly
why: The same receipt with the total 32.48 read: 8.25% added on top, as for such receipts today.

name: tax_inside_without_base_is_not_added_again
why: 内税 10% 90 with no base: 90 sits inside 1,000, so a misread amount due of 1,100 is not explained by adding 10% on top.

name: points_after_tax_with_a_tax_line_without_base
why: Tax 150 inside 1,650, then 150 of points paid: 150 is 10% on top of 1,500 and 10/110 inside 1,650, readings that disagree, so the tax line says nothing and the receipt reconciles to 1,500 paid.

name: coupon_the_printed_bases_put_on_one_rate
why: A 200 coupon with nothing printed to say which items; the bases (8%: 800, 10%: 1,000) show it was all the 8% item's. Spread over both, no split of the costs matches the bases, so a person places it.

name: sugi_subset_discount_read_without_percent_or_base
why: The 8% and the 2,909 base were not read, so the 233 is spread over every item and the snack ends at 247, but the printed 8% base is 236: the lines placed on the model's word go to a person.

adjustments.label: スギポイント値引金額

name: equal_prices_with_per_rate_bases
why: Two items at the same price and per-rate bases: some items still make up each base, so nothing changes.

name: whole_receipt_coupon_the_till_split_between_rates
why: A 101 coupon the till split 50/51 between rates while the split here is 51/50: one unit off a base per line spread over several items is a till's rounding, not a misread.

name: tax_total_read_as_a_surcharge
why: 外税 at 8% and 10% whose tax total 100 was also listed as a surcharge: it repeats the tax lines exactly, while the bases add up to the items without it, so a person removes it.

name: unnamed_percent_that_fits_an_item_and_everything_else
why: 8% of the first item's printed price is 200, and so is 8% of everything else (2,500). Two readings fit and nothing names the items, so a person decides.

name: zero_rated_vat_line
why: UK VAT: zero-rated food (0%, VAT 0.00) and a 20% item with VAT inside. A printed 0 is printed, and a 0% line says nothing about prices including tax.

name: tax_on_top_with_a_zero_tax_bag
why: 外税 at 8% and 10% where the 10% line is a 3 yen bag whose tax rounds to 0: each rate's tax goes into its own items.

name: printed_tax_one_unit_off_the_rate
why: 10% on top of 1,500 is 150 and the amount due says 150 was added, but 151 is printed as the tax: one of them was misread.

name: coupon_the_store_split_per_tax_group
why: 外税 8% and 10%: the till took 57 of a 101 coupon from the 8% group and 44 from the 10% group, here 58 and 43. The bases still single out each group within that one unit, and each rate's tax goes into its items.

name: sugi_subset_base_misread_by_one_digit
why: 2,909 read as 2,929, which three other items happen to add up to; but 8% of 2,929 is 234.32, not 233, so the line goes to a person.

adjustments.label: スギポイント値引金額

name: one_decimal_currency_kept_in_hundredths
why: A currency printed to one decimal is kept in hundredths, the precision the app checks added tax at: 8% of 10.30 is 0.82 or 0.83, not the 0.80 printed.

name: per_rate_bases_that_no_items_add_up_to
why: Per-rate bases of 800 and 1,300 on items of 100 and 2,000: no item or set of items makes 800, and nothing was placed on the model's word, so the receipt was misread.

name: per_rate_bases_printed_before_tax
why: Prices include tax but the bases are printed before it (8%: 1,000 + 80, 10%: 500 + 50): the bases with their tax are what the items make up.

name: points_after_tax_with_bases_printed_before_tax
why: The same receipt with 100 of points paid after tax: the bases describe the items before the points, which cannot be told apart from here, so they are not checked item by item.

name: bases_too_large_to_search
why: A receipt in the millions: the per-rate bases are too large to search item by item, so only their sum is checked.

name: zero_rate_line_beside_one_rate_added_on_top
why: A 0% line that taxes nothing beside 8.25% added on top (1.57 on the 19.00 left after a 1.00 coupon), and the 10% coupon fits neither item alone nor both: review. A 0% line is never the rate a client adds, so review already shows the 8.25% the receipt reconciles with once a person places the coupon.

name: points_before_tax_equal_to_the_tax_on_a_tax_exclusive_receipt
why: 1,100 on a tax-exclusive receipt, 100 of points taken off before tax and 10% added on the 1,000 left: 1,100 paid. A tax-inclusive receipt whose 100 of points were paid after tax, read with the total before them as the amount due, prints the same lines and was paid 1,000. Points equal to the tax leave nothing to tell the two apart, so neither is taken.

name: points_equal_to_the_tax_added_at_two_rates
why: 164 of points taken off before tax, then 8% and 10% added on top of the 918 left on each item (73 and 91), with no bases printed: 2,000 paid. Tax added on top at two rates explains the amount due as read, so it is not taken as a total read before the points; two rates on top go to review.

name: per_rate_base_reached_by_two_items_after_a_coupon
why: Tax added on top at 8% and 10% after a 300 coupon over the whole receipt, which leaves the items at 1,000, 1,000 and 999. The 8% base of 1,000 is the first item or the second, so its items are not known; that the third item alone comes within the one unit of rounding the coupon allows must not decide it.

name: per_rate_base_no_items_add_up_to
why: Tax added on top at 8% (12 on 150) and 10% (45 on 450): the bases add up to the items, but no set of items makes the 8% base of 150, so a base or a price was misread.

name: tax_total_read_as_a_surcharge_under_an_item
why: 外税 at 10% (120 on 1,200) whose tax was also listed as a surcharge under the second item: it repeats the tax line exactly while the base adds up to the items without it, so it is the tax read twice whichever item it was read under, and a person removes it rather than the second item's owner paying all of the tax.

name: per_rate_base_one_unit_from_one_item_after_a_coupon
why: Tax added on top at 8% (13 on 174) and 10% (52 on 523) after a 99 coupon over the whole receipt, which this module splits 25, 25 and 49: the 198 item at 173, the 200 item at 175. Only the 198 item comes within the coupon's unit of the 8% base below it, so it is the 8% item, and the 200 item a unit above must not make the base look ambiguous.
